question: Indicate which of these pathologies has predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hepatocellular necrosis -> Impaired uptake of bilirubin by hepatocytes -> Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 95% CHAIN: Dubin-Johnson syndrome -> Impaired bilirubin excretion into bile canaliculi -> Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 90% CHAIN: Gilbert's syndrome -> Defective bilirubin conjugation by UDP-glucuronosyltransferase -> Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 85% CHAIN: Intrahepatic cholestasis -> Impaired bile flow leading to accumulation of unconjugated bilirubin -> Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 95%
analysis: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia is mainly seen in conditions where there is an increased production of bilirubin or impaired uptake by the liver cells. Among the options provided, Gilbert's syndrome is known for predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia due to a defect in bilirubin conjugation process.
